text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- OECD half-yearly report sees France, Germany and Italy with a budget deficit at 3.2 percent of GDP in 1997.

-- Dutch central bank president Wim Duisenberg says in an interview a budget deficit of 3.2 percent would not be a catastrophe for countries wanting to join the single currency and a delay in implementation of the euro could be dangerous for the entire process.
Expects there to be speculative attacks on the currencies
joining the euro in the eight months to January 1, 1999. It is therefore necessary to give credible indications of the exchange rates between the euro and member currencies from May 1998.
-- Unions and employers federation opposed on whether to raise the minimum wage.
-- Rexecode economic research institute report says cost of labour hampers growth in France.
-- Insurers oppose potential agreement between La Poste and AGF to sell casualty insurance products through La Poste's network of 17,000 post offices.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Paris in grip of world stock market euphoria.
-- Electrolux "shock therapy" - to cut 12,000 jobs and close 25 plants over two years.
-- CNPF employers' federation wants lower charges on companies in exchange for wage increases.
-- France, Germany, Italy get bad marks from OECD.
-- Dell computer boss says his company could dominate the PC market by the turn of the century.
L'AGEFI
-- Poitiers summit to find a new balance in Franco-German relations.
LIBERATION
-- Generale des Eaux rules out buying TF1 television channel, currently owned by Bouygues, if it came on the market.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Electrolux decision signals that Europe's painful restructuring has yet to run its course.
